section_summary: This section continues an address list for letters from Japanese residents in Brazil to people in Japan, followed by correspondence about forwarding those letters and distributing Japanese newspapers in São Paulo. Consular reports describe film showings intended to demonstrate Japan’s defeat, violence attributed to Shindo Renmei, and one observer’s concerns about Japanese baseball clubs. A Japanese community memorial asks for clearer news from Japan; the section ends with a report that newspaper shipments remained useful and a clipping about renewed threats.

subfiles.title: Motion Picture Section trip cover despatch
subfiles.about: Cross forwards a report on film showings in Japanese communities.
subfiles.summary: Praises Alfredo P. Vasconcellos’s publicity arrangements and local Brazilian assistance.

subfiles.title: Alfredo P. Vasconcellos’s Portuguese trip report
subfiles.about: A day-by-day account of a sound-truck tour showing an occupation film and distributing Japanese papers.
subfiles.summary: The crew visited Sorocaba, Piraju, Rancharia, Presidente Prudente, Presidente Bernardes, Álvares Machado and Bastos in December 1946. Attendance varied, while Japanese volunteers often feared being seen explaining the film because of Shindo Renmei threats. The report records local publicity, police help and travel expenses.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of newspapers, despatch 13
subfiles.about: The Consul General acknowledges three late-1946 newspaper shipments.
subfiles.summary: Confirms receipt of all enclosed Japanese papers.

subfiles.title: Attempted murder of Paulo Morita
subfiles.about: Cross reports an attack intended for Paulo Morita, who handled Japanese consular work.
subfiles.summary: Attackers reportedly killed a man in Morita’s home by mistake; his child escaped. Cross attributes the attack to Tokotai members.

subfiles.title: Translation of film tour report, cover despatch 10
subfiles.about: Cross sends a translated film-tour report and a newspaper article about a São Paulo murder.
subfiles.summary: He finds belief in Japanese victory weakened but calls for more films and newspapers showing conditions in occupied Japan.

subfiles.title: Jornal Trabalhista clipping on murder in Aclimação
subfiles.about: A newspaper account says attackers seeking Paulo Morita killed his brother-in-law.
subfiles.summary: The article attributes the attack to Tokotai, described as part of Shindo Renmei, and says suspects were arrested. Its later OCR includes fragments of unrelated nearby stories.

subfiles.title: English translation of Alta Sorocabana film-tour report
subfiles.from: Motion Picture Section, American Consulate General
subfiles.about: An English translation records screenings of a film about the American occupation of Japan.
subfiles.summary: The sound truck visited communities across Alta Sorocabana from December 11 to 21, 1946. The report gives attendance and newspaper distribution figures and describes local support. It repeatedly notes Japanese residents’ fear of publicly explaining the film because of Shindo Renmei intimidation.

subfiles.title: Observations on the Japanese Problem in São Paulo, Brazil
subfiles.from: Unnamed baseball league secretary and observer
subfiles.about: An observer describes Japanese baseball networks and proposes using integrated clubs to influence younger Japanese Brazilians.
subfiles.summary: The writer estimates 271 clubs and about 800 teams, maps their locations, and describes contacts with Toshio Oda and Tomio Takeda. He alleges that older Japanese leaders used baseball to maintain political discipline, distinguishing first, second and third generations. He proposes a field, games, press, radio, publications and school teams to draw younger players into Brazilian-American clubs. These claims are the writer’s assessment.

subfiles.summary: Leaders accepting Japan’s defeat request transmission of their memorial; an English résumé accompanies it.

subfiles.title: English résumé of Japanese community memorial
subfiles.from: Japanese community leaders in São Paulo
subfiles.about: The memorial seeks measures to counter violent disbelief in Japan’s defeat among Japanese residents of Brazil.
subfiles.summary: It reports murders, injuries and disturbances through January 1947. Proposed measures include regional Japanese newspapers, explicit letters, radio broadcasts, religious-group messages and a mission from Japan. It lists attached reports on a public-information campaign, Shindo Renmei violence and organization, expulsions, and Brazilian reactions.

subfiles.title: Department file note on missing memorial

subfiles.summary: Action is deferred pending receipt of the memorial.

subfiles.summary: Encloses a copy of despatch 210 and its stated enclosures.

subfiles.title: Request to continue Japanese newspaper shipments, despatch 333
subfiles.about: The Consulate requests Japanese newspapers through at least July.
subfiles.summary: It credits the papers with helping calm violence in inland São Paulo, says conditions remain unsettled, and encloses a Shindo Renmei clipping.

subfiles.title: A Noite clipping on renewed Shindo Renmei threats
subfiles.about: The article reports a renewed Shindo Renmei campaign of threats against Japanese Brazilians who accepted Japan’s defeat.
subfiles.summary: It alleges that police detained Minoru Mirata, identified as a secretary of the reorganized group, and found badges and a forged account claiming Brazil had been ceded to Japan. It describes death threats and continuing police inquiries. The article continues beyond the supplied text.
